findings.title: Thresholds reverse-engineered so 10 known 2024-26 winners pass (anchor-fitting)
findings.file: CONTEXT.md; methods/revenue-growth-3y.js; methods/rule-of-40.js; methods/quality-compounder-roic.js; methods/reinvestment-rate.js; methods/score-aggregator.js; methods/r40-sanity-cap.js
findings.line_range: CONTEXT.md 78-92; revenue-growth-3y.js 1-14; rule-of-40.js 59-79; quality-compounder-roic.js 10-43; reinvestment-rate.js 20-42; score-aggregator.js 235-248
findings.description: The binding rule 'never exclude an anchor to pass a guard; fix the guard' (CONTEXT.md) institutionalizes calibrating the methodology until NVDA/MSFT/PLTR/META/COST/GOOG/AVGO/V/CRDO/MELI all PASS. These anchors are known ex-post winners of the 2024-2026 AI-led regime. Concrete instances: revenue-growth-3y threshold lowered 25%->22% explicitly because 'AVGO 24.4% and NOW 22.4% missed HG by 0.6pp/2.6pp'; rule-of-40 got a TTM-negative->3y-median FCF fallback capped at -20pp because MELI's case was -12.9pp (boundary set just past the anchor); quality-compounder-roic grew a 15%-ROIC 'retail tier' for the COST pattern; reinvestment-rate got a 5% financials override because 'V failed the QC MUST gate at 5.7%'; HG coverage floor lowered 40%->30% so CRDO/ALAB/PLTR-era IPOs survive; r40-sanity-cap F2 set at fcfMargin>80% because 'no anchor exceeds 50%'. hypergrowth-quality-class tier thresholds carry ticker comments (CRDO/ALAB/RDDT for >50% quarters; APP/NOW/MELI/ANET for >25%).
findings.mechanism: Each calibration is a one-sided update: a threshold only ever moves when a known winner fails it; there is no symmetric procedure that tightens a threshold when a known loser passes. Over ~120 tags of iteration this performs implicit in-sample optimization on a 10-stock positive-label set with zero negative labels, fitting the screener to the profile of the last regime's winners.
findings.reproducer: grep -n 'anchor' methods/*.js CONTEXT.md | grep -i 'fix\|repair\|admit\|lower' — every hit is a threshold moved to admit a named anchor; tests/integration-anchor-test.js enforces 10/10 anchors PASS as a CI gate.
findings.impact: The screener's discrimination is certified only on stocks already known to have gone up; forward rankings are tilted toward 2024-26-winner lookalikes (AI hardware/megacap-platform profile). In a regime rotation (e.g. a 2021-22-style derating, which the knowledge base flags as the key failure mode) the calibration is untested and likely mis-ranked. The anchor test then actively prevents recalibration because any tightening that fails an anchor is forbidden.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep anchors as regression fixtures but add (a) a negative-anchor set (known blowups: e.g. 2021 cohort SaaS deraters, SPAC-era fakes) that must FAIL, and (b) a rule that any threshold change motivated by an anchor must also be validated on walk-forward forward-return spread, not just on anchor pass/fail.

findings.title: HYPERGROWTH score collapses to ~2 factors; growth enters 4 of 6 weighted inputs
findings.description: SCORE_WEIGHTS.HYPERGROWTH: rule-of-40 0.25 (growth+fcfMargin), rule-of-x 0.10 (2*growth+fcfMargin, SAME two inputs), revenue-growth-3y 0.15 (growth), profitability-state 0.20 (margin/profit state), hypergrowth-quality-class 0.20 (quarterly growth breadth + OI direction), gross-margin-stability 0.10. Revenue growth drives ~0.70 of weight, FCF/operating margin ~0.65 (overlapping). rule-of-40 and rule-of-x are near-duplicates computed from literally the same two fields (revenueGrowthYoY, fcfMarginTTM) and jointly carry 0.35. The in-code comment ('revenue triple-counted via R40+RoX+rev-3y; redistributed') acknowledges the issue but the fix only trimmed revenue-growth-3y; the R40/RoX duplication remains. Across all modes, the 98 registered methods reduce to ~16 scored CORE inputs, which map onto roughly 5 underlying factors (revenue growth, margin level/state, ROIC, balance-sheet risk, earnings stability); the other ~70 DIAGNOSTIC methods carry zero weight.
findings.mechanism: Equal/fixed weighting of highly correlated signals concentrates effective weight: with corr(R40,RoX) near 1 and both correlated with revenue-growth-3y and hypergrowth-quality-class, the effective factor loading on 'recent revenue growth' is far above any single stated weight - a hidden mega-weight the weight table does not disclose.
findings.reproducer: Compute pairwise correlations of method values across snapshots: rule-of-40.value vs rule-of-x.value = corr ~0.99 by construction (value_x = value_40 + growth); both share fcfMarginTTM exactly.
findings.impact: HG ranking is, to first order, a momentum-free revenue-growth sort with a margin tiebreak. The knowledge base grades raw growth level as a NON-persistent, non-predictive input (Chan-Karceski-Lakonishok) and warns that rewarding big revenue increases buys the asset-growth-anomaly losers. The apparent diversification of 6 weighted methods is illusory.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop one of rule-of-40/rule-of-x from the weights (keep the other as display), or orthogonalize: weight one growth-efficiency composite (Rule-of-X style), one growth-quality input, one valuation input, one dilution input - per the 4-pillar skeleton in the evidence base.

findings.title: Evidence-STRONG factors carry zero weight; MIXED/WEAK Rule-of-40 carries the most
findings.description: The project's own evidence base (Jarvis/Knowledge/Trading/growth-screener/factor-evidence-foundations.md) grades gross profitability (Novy-Marx), asset growth (Cooper-Gulen-Schill, negative), and net share issuance/dilution as the THREE robust STRONG return predictors, and grades Rule-of-40-as-return-predictor MIXED/WEAK. In the screener: gross-profitability is DIAGNOSTIC (weight 0), asset-growth-anomaly is DIAGNOSTIC (weight 0; only the rev-relative sibling asset-growth-divergence acts as a -8pt soft guard in QC only), and ALL dilution signals (sbc-revenue, sbc-trend, sbc-growth-ratio, buyback-yield, capex-vs-sbc-quality, rule-of-40-sbc-adjusted) are DIAGNOSTIC with weight 0. The dilution red flag promised in score-aggregator.js ('Tag 121+: Dilution-Red-Flag wenn Share-Outstanding-Daten verfuegbar') was never implemented - RED_FLAG_RULES contains only HIGH_DEBT and EXTREME_SLOAN. Meanwhile rule-of-40 + rule-of-x carry 0.35 of the HG score and the R40 tab is the default UI surface.
findings.mechanism: The score is built almost entirely from health/heuristic signals (R40, profitability state, margin stability) while the replicated cross-sectional return predictors sit unscored in detail modals. A stock diluting 8%/yr with ballooning assets and weak gross profitability loses zero score points in any mode as long as growth and margins look good - exactly the false-positive profile the evidence base says kills growth portfolios.
findings.reproducer: grep -n "'sbc\|gross-profitability\|asset-growth" methods/score-aggregator.js returns nothing in SCORE_WEIGHTS or RED_FLAG_RULES; method-types.js shows all typed DIAGNOSTIC.
findings.impact: Material adverse selection at the top of the rankings: SBC-heavy software with optical FCF and acquisition-driven growers can reach Tier A. This is the single largest gap between the screener and its own commissioned evidence base.
findings.suggested_fix: Add three scored inputs (or red-flag downgrades) with modest weights: share-count CAGR penalty (first-class per evidence), GP/assets floor, total-asset-growth penalty. Wire the existing DIAGNOSTIC methods in via SCORE_WEIGHTS after a fixture-hash bless, or at minimum implement the promised dilution RED_FLAG rule.

findings.title: Default UI is a raw Rule-of-40 magnitude ranking; HG/QC score tabs hidden
findings.description: filter-config.json sets ui.defaultTab='R40' and hiddenTabs=['HG','QC'] - the entire mode-score/tier machinery is hidden by default and the user lands on a list ranked by raw R40 value (tabs.R40.sort by r40*(1-penalty)). The SMALL tab ranks purely by raw revenue growth (sort (b.growth - a.growth)). The evidence base states explicitly: the single 40 threshold is arbitrary and binary; R40 magnitude correlates with the valuation multiple the market already pays (i.e. how expensive a stock is), not with forward alpha; and ranking by raw growth is the asset-growth-anomaly trap. The R40 tab does add a durability gate (>=3 of last 4 quarters over 40), which helps, but the ordering criterion remains R40 magnitude.
findings.mechanism: Sorting descending by growth+margin systematically promotes the most-loved, most-expensive names at the moment their fundamentals are most extrapolated, with zero valuation or dilution input anywhere in the ordering.
findings.reproducer: Open screener.html: default tab R40, top rows ordered by the R40 composite. filter-config.json ui block confirms HG/QC hidden.
findings.impact: Whatever validity the (more diversified) mode scores have is bypassed in the primary user surface; the de-facto product is the construct the evidence base was commissioned to replace.
findings.suggested_fix: Make a mode-score tab the default; keep R40 as a column/filter, not a ranking. If R40 must rank, rank by score-within-R40-qualifiers or by growth-adjusted valuation residual.

findings.title: Missing-data renormalization lets thin-coverage stocks score 100 from 2 signals
findings.description: computeScore normalizes the weighted sum by computedWeight (weight of computable methods only) and the HG coverage floor was lowered to 0.30 specifically so recent IPOs pass. Consequence: a 2-year-old company where only rule-of-40 (0.25) and rule-of-x (0.10) are computable clears the 0.30 floor and is scored 100*(s40*0.25+sX*0.10)/0.35 - i.e. its ENTIRE HG score is two near-duplicate signals from the same two fields; if both pass it scores 100 and outranks a fully-covered company that passes 5 of 6 methods (score ~80-90). Incomputable DATAGUARDs are likewise treated as neutral (guards only fire when computable=true), so less data also means fewer hard/soft hurdles. Mode-eval marks missing guards only as text warnings.
findings.mechanism: Renormalization treats 'no data' as 'average of observed signals' rather than as uncertainty; combined with guard skip-on-incomputable, expected score is non-decreasing as coverage falls for any stock whose observable signals are its strongest ones (the typical recent-IPO hypergrowth case).
findings.reproducer: Construct a snapshot with only revenueGrowthYoY=60 and fcfMarginTTM=5 (no annual arrays): rule-of-40=65 pass, rule-of-x=125 pass, gross-margin-stability/hypergrowth-quality-class/profitability-state incomputable -> computedWeight=0.35>=0.30 -> score=100, Tier A.
findings.impact: Systematic upward bias for young, thin-history, unprofitable names - the highest-risk cohort - and a direct violation of the evidence-base rule that missing data should 'normalize over available pillars + set a coverage flag - never penalize' WITH a visible coverage cap; here it silently rewards. Tier A becomes a mix of proven names and 2-signal unknowns presented identically.
findings.suggested_fix: Cap the score by coverage (e.g. score_max = 100*computedWeight/totalWeight + small slack), or display tier with a coverage suffix (A vs A?) and never rank a sub-50%-coverage stock above a full-coverage stock at equal score.

findings.title: Key numeric constants have no empirical provenance; tuning tool optimizes pass-rates, not returns
findings.description: Provenance audit of the load-bearing numbers: Rule-of-40 threshold 40 = practitioner folklore (the evidence base itself grades it a health heuristic, not a return predictor). Rule-of-X threshold 58 with multiplier 2.0 - Bessemer published 2.3 and no threshold; 58 appears nowhere in the cited literature (it is what makes a 2.0-multiplier RoX roughly as selective as R40>=40 on the current universe). Tier boundaries 80/65/50 are round numbers from a 'Tag 117/120 Triple-AI Battle' (an LLM debate, not data). SOFT_GUARD_PENALTY points (8/10/7/6/8/6/5) same provenance. PRE_BREAKOUT pbScore weights (25/20/15/10/15/15) hand-set. ROIC bars 20/17/15 with AT overrides set in council consensus then patched per anchor (F-MD-001). The only tuning tool, tune-threshold.js, sweeps a threshold +/-50% and reports PASS-RATES on today's snapshot cross-section - it contains no forward-return objective at all, so any threshold 'tuned' with it was fit to pass-count aesthetics on the current in-sample universe.
findings.mechanism: Thresholds chosen for selectivity-on-today's-universe are a form of in-sample fitting that silently re-fits as the universe drifts, and none of them has been tested against the only ground truth that matters (forward return spread of pass vs fail).
findings.reproducer: Read tune-threshold.js lines 42-67: the sweep output is {threshold, pass, ratio} only. outputs/method-effectiveness.md (the return-spread report) is empty of any qualifying method.
findings.impact: Wasted complexity and unwarranted confidence: dozens of precise-looking constants encode editorial taste. Severity limited to MEDIUM because most thresholds gate graduated scores rather than hard-exclude (except DATAGUARDs).
findings.suggested_fix: For each CORE threshold, record provenance (paper / consensus / anchor-fit / pass-rate-fit) in the method header, and add forward-return spread to tune-threshold.js output so future tuning has an empirical objective.

findings.title: No demonstrated predictive edge: effectiveness tables empty, only long backtest is negative
findings.description: The project's own validation layer currently shows: (1) outputs/method-effectiveness.md - the 28d and 84d per-method alpha tables are EMPTY (no method clears the min-vintage/min-sample evidence gate); (2) outputs/walk-forward.md - 7 vintages, only 7d horizons populated, alphas -0.10 to -0.25pp (noise-level, slightly negative), 28d/84d horizons have zero vintages; (3) the only longer-horizon test, backtest-10w-result.json (70d), shows alphaAvg = -12.4pp and alphaMed = -6.0pp (pass-cohort UNDERPERFORMED the fail-cohort), and its own header admits forward-looking bias in the method values. Despite this, 16 methods are promoted CORE with fixed weights, tiers are published daily, and the README presents the mode system as established. The evidence base's binding rule 9 ('validate per sector via walk-forward before promoting to CORE') has not been satisfied for any method, and McLean-Pontiff decay (haircut ~50%) is cited in the KB but applied nowhere.
findings.mechanism: Weights and tiers were locked by consensus before the measurement infrastructure had any statistical power; the single completed measurement points the wrong way and triggered no methodology change.
findings.reproducer: type outputs\method-effectiveness.md - both tables have headers and zero rows. type backtest-10w-result.json | findstr alpha.
findings.impact: Every downstream artifact (tiers, top picks, Discord alerts) communicates a ranking whose predictive validity is unmeasured at best and measured-negative in the one available long-horizon sample. This is the central open question for the whole project.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat current weights as hypotheses: freeze them, accumulate 28d/84d vintages until the effectiveness gate populates, then re-weight via the planned semi-automatic review (IMPROVEMENT-PLAN #4) with the KB's 50% haircut. Surface 'predictive validity: unvalidated' in the report header until then.

findings.title: Score saturates at thresholds; Tier-A ranking differences are mostly noise
findings.description: normalizeMethodScore returns exactly 1.0 for any pass - a stock at 200% of a threshold scores identically to one at 101% - and graduates only below threshold. Strong stocks therefore pile up at/near 100 and within-tier-A ordering is driven by which methods happened to be computable (F-MD-005), soft-guard point deductions, and sub-threshold partial credits, not by fundamental strength differences. The modes report and screener tabs nevertheless present a strictly ordered Top-200 with integer scores and day-over-day delta-score badges, implying that 87 vs 84 is a meaningful distinction. Tier boundaries (80/65/50) create cliff effects where a 1-point data wiggle moves a stock between 'B' and 'NEAR_MISS' labels that read as investment categories.
findings.mechanism: A sum of saturated step-ish functions has very low resolution among qualifying stocks; presenting it as a 0-100 cardinal scale with sorted lists and deltas overstates the information content by an order of magnitude.
findings.reproducer: For any two stocks passing all 6 HG methods the score is exactly 100 regardless of 30% vs 120% growth; ordering between them falls to ticker-compare in generate-screener.js sorts.
findings.impact: Users chart-time allocation (the screener's one job per the KB handoff note) is steered by pseudo-precision; genuinely stronger stocks get no headroom above weaker qualifiers.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend graduation above threshold (e.g. cap at 1.2-1.5x credit with diminishing returns) or add a within-tier sort key based on a continuous composite (e.g. Rule-of-X magnitude, sector percentile), and drop delta-score badges for changes < 5.

findings.title: Absolute/relative inversion: quality bars drift to universe medians, valuation never relative
findings.description: The evidence base prescribes: quality gates ABSOLUTE (a quality bar should not weaken because the universe weakened), valuation RELATIVE (cheap-for-its-growth vs sector regression). The screener implements the inverse on both sides. Quality: fcf-yield and roic pass through effectiveThreshold, which (per sibling finding F-ME-201) silently replaces the documented absolute bars (5% / 15%) with the rolling median of the screener's OWN growth-skewed universe (e.g. HARDWARE fcf-yield 0.81%, BANK roic 0.98%) - so the QC 'quality' inputs degrade into 'above median of a partially loss-making watchlist'. Valuation: there is NO relative valuation anywhere - no EV/Gross-Profit, no EV/Sales-vs-growth regression residual (the KB's designated value pillar), no sector percentile; HYPERGROWTH carries zero valuation weight and QC only the (now relative) fcf-yield at 0.05. The only valuation feedback a user sees in HG is a text warning 'Bewertung sehr ambitioniert' when fcf-yield < 2%.
findings.mechanism: Universe-relative quality bars are pro-cyclical (a frothy universe lowers the bar exactly when it should rise); absent growth-adjusted valuation, the score cannot distinguish a compounder at 8x GP from the same compounder at 40x GP.
findings.reproducer: See findings/methods-engine.json F-ME-201 reproducer for the relative-quality flip; grep -rn 'EV' methods/*.js shows only ev-ebitda (defaultActive:false, DIAGNOSTIC).
findings.impact: QC quality discrimination weakens with universe drift, and across all modes the screener is structurally blind to price - it will rank an identical business identically at any valuation, which the KB calls the trap that the value lamp must catch.
findings.suggested_fix: Floor quality thresholds at a fraction of the documented absolute bar (per F-ME-201), and implement the KB value pillar: per-sector regression of EV/GP (or EV/Sales) on growth, scored as residual; even as a DIAGNOSTIC lamp first.

findings.title: Hard filters contradict the rank-and-warn principle: Sloan hard-gate and broad sector deletes
findings.description: sloan-ratio is a hard DATAGUARD in every mode's dataGuards[] (fail = stock invisible in that mode), although the evidence base grades the accruals anomaly MIXED/decayed and prescribes 'red flags are graded penalties + visible warning lamps, never silent hard deletes'. The 2-consecutive-year escalation softens it, but MELI was invisible for months on exactly this gate until a sign-aware patch - demonstrating the false-negative cost the KB warns about. Separately, whole sectors are regex-hard-excluded per mode (HG: all mining/metals/oil&gas/healthcare-plans; QC additionally: steel, autos, airlines, utilities, telecom), which silently deletes any genuine winner in those industries (e.g. a 2020-22-class energy compounder cycle would have been invisible to every mode except TURNAROUND/BUFFETT).
findings.mechanism: Hard gates convert model uncertainty into silent recall loss; the user never sees what was deleted, so the error is invisible and uncorrectable - the exact asymmetry the KB's design-rule 7 forbids.
findings.reproducer: strategy-modes.js SECTOR_EXCLUDE_QC includes /utilities|telecom/; any utility scores null in QC regardless of fundamentals. MELI case documented in score-aggregator.js EXTREME_SLOAN comment.
findings.impact: Recall loss concentrated in unfashionable sectors and accrual-noisy business models (consumer credit, marketplaces); medium because the WATCH/R40 tabs partially backstop visibility.
findings.suggested_fix: Demote sloan-ratio from mode dataGuards to soft-guard penalty + lamp (keep the 2-year hard rule only at extreme levels), and convert sector excludes into mode-fit penalties or visible 'wrong-mode' badges instead of deletes.

findings.title: 3y revenue CAGR weighted CORE while acceleration signals sit unweighted, inverting persistence evidence
findings.description: Chan-Karceski-Lakonishok (graded STRONG in the evidence base) shows multi-year growth does not persist, and the KB's design rule says 'weight recent trend/acceleration, not a long CAGR'. The screener does the opposite: revenue-growth-3y (a 3y CAGR with a hard 22% bar) is CORE-weighted in HYPERGROWTH (0.15) and TURNAROUND (0.10) and is a hard MUST for the HG passed flag, while the acceleration family - revenue-acceleration-yoy, quarterly-revenue-acceleration, earnings-surprise-momentum (PEAD, the strongest near-term fundamental signal in the KB) - are all DIAGNOSTIC with zero weight. hypergrowth-quality-class partially encodes recent breadth, mitigating but not curing the imbalance.
findings.mechanism: Weighting the non-persistent level over the persistent short-horizon change means the score is slowest to recognize both inflections the user cares about: fresh acceleration (entry) and deceleration (exit) - deceleration enters only as a -10pt soft guard.
findings.reproducer: A company re-accelerating from 10%->35% YoY with 3y CAGR 18% fails revenue-growth-3y (hard MUST) and cannot pass HG; a decelerating 60%->25% with 3y CAGR 45% passes everything minus a 10-point soft penalty.
findings.impact: Systematically late entries and exits relative to an evidence-aligned weighting; the Elliott-handoff loses exactly the 'accelerating fundamentals + early wave' setups the KB calls highest-conviction.
findings.suggested_fix: Swap roles: make a recent-trend/acceleration composite the weighted input and demote the 3y CAGR to a context DIAGNOSTIC, or at least remove revenue-growth-3y from the hard MUST list.

findings.title: BUFFETT mode: 50% weight on one 14-test composite plus 30% on automated DCF
findings.description: SCORE_WEIGHTS.BUFFETT = buffett-criteria 0.50, dcf-intrinsic-value 0.30, owner-earnings 0.20. Half the score is a single opaque 14-sub-test composite (sub-tests internally equal-ish weighted, pass at 85%), and 30% is a 3-stage DCF whose output is dominated by hardcoded assumptions: growth clamped to max 15%, discount floor 9%, terminal growth 2.5%, 7+5 year stages, 25%/50% margin-of-safety buckets, 15% hurdle. The evidence base grades automated reverse-DCF 'WEAK (for automation) - modal diagnostic, not weighted'. Composite-of-composites scoring also hides which factor actually moved the score (the project's own stated reason for preferring reason-codes over aggregates in hypergrowth-quality-class).
findings.mechanism: With a 0.50 single-input weight, the mode's ranking variance is dominated by one method's internal sub-threshold choices; the DCF adds assumption noise dressed as precision (intrinsic-value point estimates from clamped CAGRs).
findings.reproducer: Any change to one buffett-criteria sub-test moves 50% of the mode score; dcf-intrinsic-value output flips on the 15% growth clamp for any company with historical CAGR above it.
findings.impact: BUFFETT-mode tiers carry an authority ('literaturgestuetzt') their construction does not support; medium since the mode is secondary in the UI.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-weight toward the separately observable components (owner-earnings growth, debt, ROIC trend) and demote the DCF margin-of-safety to a lamp/diagnostic as the KB prescribes.

findings.title: README documents superseded HYPERGROWTH/QC weights and omits BUFFETT mode
findings.description: README's strategy-mode tables show rule-of-40 0.25 / revenue-growth-3y 0.25 / profitability-state 0.15 / hypergrowth-quality-class 0.15 and a QC list including above-200d-ma at 0.05; the live SCORE_WEIGHTS are revenue-growth-3y 0.15, profitability-state 0.20, hypergrowth-quality-class 0.20, QC without above-200d-ma (earnings-stability 0.20), plus an entire BUFFETT mode absent from the README. Anyone auditing the methodology from the documentation reasons about the wrong model.
findings.mechanism: Doc drift after the redistribution commit; the methodology surface (the thing reviewed by humans) and the executed weights diverged.
findings.reproducer: diff README.md mode tables against SCORE_WEIGHTS in methods/score-aggregator.js.
findings.impact: Cosmetic but corrosive to trust in the stated methodology; also hides the (positive) removal of the technical signal from QC.
findings.suggested_fix: Generate the README weight tables from SCORE_WEIGHTS at build time, or add a CI check comparing them.
